title: Mexican Rice
subtitle: tomato-cooked red rice with peas
excerpt: Rice toasted in oil then cooked in a tomato and stock base until fluffy and red. Peas go in at the end. This is the classic side dish for tacos, enchiladas, or any Mexican meal.
sourceNotes: Mexican rice, or arroz rojo, is a staple side dish across Mexico. The tomato-enriched colour and flavour come from frying the rice in oil before adding the liquid, a technique that prevents sticking.

content.text: Toast the dry rice in oil until golden before adding any liquid. This step is what gives Mexican rice its distinct texture and stops it going mushy. Do not stir once the liquid goes in -- let it steam with the lid on.
Heat the oil in a wide saucepan over medium heat. Add the dry rice and stir for 3 to 4 minutes until golden and toasted.
Add the onion and garlic. Cook for 2 minutes.
Stir in the cumin, tomato puree, and blended tinned tomatoes.
Pour in the stock. Season with salt. Bring to a boil.
Reduce to a low simmer. Put the lid on and cook for 15 minutes without lifting the lid.
Scatter the peas over the surface. Put the lid back on and rest off the heat for 5 minutes.
Fluff with a fork and serve.

items.cause: Lid lifted during cooking or too much liquid
items.fix: Do not lift the lid during the 15-minute steam. Use a 5:3 liquid-to-rice ratio by volume.

items.symptom: Rice is catching on the base
items.cause: Heat too high or not enough oil initially
items.fix: Keep the heat low after adding the stock. Use a heavy-based pan if possible.

items.cause: Not enough tomato or tomatoes not blended
items.fix: Blend the tinned tomatoes until smooth before adding. Add an extra tablespoon of tomato puree for a deeper colour.

content.text: Arroz rojo is eaten daily across Mexico. Every region and every family has their own version. The technique of toasting dry rice in fat before adding liquid came to Mexico from Spanish and Arab cooking traditions. Today it is served alongside almost every main dish in Mexican cooking from tacos to carnitas.
